title: Implement short/long request classification (scheduler) + config wiring + rollout gating
creator: Lena Fischer
description:
Goal
- Add request classification logic (short vs long) used by the mixed-workload scheduler prototype.
- Wire classification thresholds + policy toggles through runtime config (per pool / per model defaults).
- Add acceptance/regression tests and gating so we can safely canary.

Context
- Mixed workloads (short chat prompts + long-context prompts) cause p95 tail latency spikes due to head-of-line blocking.
- The two-queue dispatch work (ENG-2438) depends on a stable, debuggable classifier with safe bounds and an easy rollback.

Scope
1) Classification criteria
- Input signals:
  - prompt_tokens (prefill length)
  - requested max_new_tokens
  - optional: predicted_prefill_ms (if available from estimator)
- Initial heuristic (proposal): classify as LONG if prompt_tokens >= short_long_prompt_threshold_tokens OR predicted_prefill_ms >= short_long_prefill_threshold_ms.
- Default thresholds to come from trace analysis (ENG-2421) and can be overridden per pool.

2) Config wiring
- Add config keys (names TBD but must be consistent with runtime config conventions):
  - scheduler.mixed_workload.enabled (feature flag)
  - scheduler.classification.enabled
  - scheduler.classification.short_long_prompt_threshold_tokens
  - scheduler.classification.short_long_prefill_threshold_ms
  - scheduler.classification.force_class (debug only; OFF by default; requires allowlist)
- Config must be plumbed from pool config -> runtime instance -> scheduler.
- Validation: enforce safe bounds (e.g., threshold_tokens in [64, 16384], threshold_ms in [1, 2000]) to prevent foot-guns.

3) Rollout gating / safety
- Hard disable path: if scheduler.mixed_workload.enabled == false OR classification.enabled == false, classifier returns legacy behavior (single class).
- Add metrics tag on request: scheduler_class={short|long|unknown} and a counter for unknown/missing prompt_tokens.
- Ensure no PII logging: only token counts / class label.

4) Acceptance tests
- Unit tests for classification edge cases:
  - missing prompt_tokens -> unknown (treated as long by default OR conservative path; pick one and document)
  - exact boundary values
  - estimator present vs absent
  - debug override requires allowlist / build flag
- Integration test (runtime scheduler harness):
  - feed synthetic requests with known token lengths
  - assert classification labels appear in emitted trace/metrics payload

Out of scope
- Any customer-facing QoS tiering beyond internal short/long.
- Dynamic per-request reprioritization based on user tier (future).

Success criteria
- Classification is stable (no flapping across retries) and explainable via logs/metrics.
- Config changes can be rolled out pool-by-pool and reverted quickly.
- Does not regress baseline throughput when mixed scheduler is disabled.

Links
- Design doc (Confluence): sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/mixed-workload-scheduler-prototype-design.json
- ADR (Confluence): sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-short-long-prompt-scheduling-policy.json
comments: 2025-12-10 (Lena Fischer): Creating implementation ticket for classifier + config plumbing. Two-queue dispatch depends on this being solid + observable. Please keep the classification logic simple and conservative for prototype (we can iterate after perf-canary data).

2025-12-12 (Marcus Reed): Drafted classifier API: classify(RequestContext) -> {SHORT,LONG,UNKNOWN} plus reason enum for debug (threshold_tokens, threshold_ms, missing_tokens, override). Keeping reason only in debug logs to avoid metric cardinality.

2025-12-13 (Benji Okafor): Config plumbing approach: add scheduler.classification.* keys to runtime config schema, allow override per pool + per model. I’ll handle validation + defaults; Marcus can consume typed config in scheduler init.

2025-12-16 (Omar El-Sayed): Note: prompt_tokens is not always known at enqueue time for some request types (streaming + tool calls). Please ensure we compute tokens early or have a deterministic fallback. Conservative fallback should be LONG to protect p95 for short traffic, but we need to confirm starvation guardrails in ENG-2438/ENG-24905.

2025-12-18 (Lena Fischer): Decision: if prompt_tokens missing, classify as LONG (conservative) AND increment scheduler_classification_missing_prompt_tokens_total. Add a short-term TODO to improve tokenization availability earlier in pipeline.

2025-12-20 (Marcus Reed): Implemented unit tests for boundary conditions + missing tokens behavior. Added integration test that asserts scheduler_class label exists on trace span 'runtime.scheduler.enqueue'.
2025-12-23 (Marcus Reed): Open question: do we gate debug override behind build tag or config allowlist? Proposal: require both (build tag + allowlisted pool id) to avoid accidental prod usage.

2025-12-26 (Allison Grant): From observability side: please ensure metric names match existing conventions and do not add high-cardinality labels. Class label is fine (short/long/unknown). Reason enum should not be a label.
2026-01-02 (Marcus Reed): PR up for review; includes config schema + typed plumbing + tests. Still need final sign-off from Lena + Benji on bounds/defaults.

2026-01-07 (Lena Fischer): Reviewed PR; requested one change: document threshold defaults + rationale in code comment and in runtime config docs. Also ensure 'unknown' never routes to SHORT implicitly.
